title: Sri Rudram (Namakam & Chamakam)

work.title: Śrī Rudram — Namakam and Chamakam (Rudrapraśna, Śatarudrīya)

sources.label: Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5 and 4.7, pañcāśat text with svara (W1), github.com/vishvAsa/vedAH_yajuH — saMhitA/mUlam/panchAti-kramaH
sources.note: The base text. The corpus records it as keyed from TITUS and Parankuśācārya's edition. Three mis-keyings corrected and logged (rudramchamakam/edition/corrections.json).

sources.label: Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5 and 4.7, vākya text in Weber's orthography (W2), github.com/vishvAsa/vedAH_yajuH — saMhitA/mUlam/vAkya-kramaH
sources.note: Independently keyed second witness; collated letter by letter and svara by svara.

sources.label: Sāyaṇa, bhāṣya on Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.5 and 4.7, github.com/vishvAsa/vedAH_yajuH — saMhitA/sarva-prastutiH
sources.note: The authority for the traditional notes; every Sanskrit phrase quoted from it is checked against it. Its yajus counts fix the units of Namakam 2–9.

sources.label: Abhinava Śaṅkara, Śrīrudrabhāṣyam (Śrī Vāṇī Vilāsa Press, Śrīraṅgam, 2nd ed. 1962), transcribed in github.com/vishvAsa/vedAH_yajuH
sources.note: Printed text of the Namakam with commentary; third witness where W1 and W2 differ.

sources.label: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (O. Hellwig), TS 4.5.1–2, github.com/OliverHellwig/sanskrit
Monier-Williams, Sanskrit-English Dictionary (Cologne digital edition), github.com/sanskrit-lexicon/csl-orig

translation.note: The padaccheda, word tables, sandhi, samāsa and grammar notes, translations and the English traditional notes were prepared for PaddySpeaks in the 2026-10 study edition (rudramchamakam/edition/analysis/). They are not taken from a published translation; the traditional notes report Sāyaṇa, reflections are labelled modern, and doubtful points are flagged.

statusNote: The Sanskrit is verified against two independently keyed witnesses, Sāyaṇa's bhāṣya and (for the Namakam) a printed commentary, and every padaccheda is proven; the svara layer and the flagged readings await review by a qualified Vedic scholar.

verification.method: Automated proof: text.json equals the base witness with exactly the logged corrections; the collation with the second witness yields exactly the classified differences; unit counts equal Sāyaṇa's ṛk and yajus counts; every padaccheda rejoins by external sandhi into the Saṃhitā; every word table matches its padaccheda; every IAST string survives the round trip; every Sanskrit quotation in the traditional notes occurs in Sāyaṇa.

Letter-by-letter collation of W1 and W2 (after documented spelling equivalences) and syllable-by-syllable comparison of their svara; every letter difference arbitrated by Sāyaṇa and Abhinava Śaṅkara and logged.
Audit of the previous page against the verified text (missing and extra words, the omitted च मे refrain, sandhi, transliteration, word coverage, unsupported interpretation).
verification.scope: the page as it stood before 2026-10-13 (rudramchamakam/edition/legacy/data.json)

knownIssues.summary: Svara: the syllables where W1 and W2 mark the accent differently are flagged on their units and listed on /rudramchamakam/sources.html#svara; they need a qualified reciter's or scholar's check.
Readings and interpretations flagged 'uncertain' or 'variant' are listed under 'Open questions' on /rudramchamakam/sources.html#open.
The traditional pada-pāṭha of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā was not available; the padaccheda is a learner's word division, proven against the Saṃhitā but not the attested pada text.
